newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX May falls to fresh low, but downside limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX May falls to fresh low, but downside limited.

text.p: May Brent fell to fresh lows on SIMEX as the contract played catch-up with losses in late NYMEX trading.
But brokers said they doubted there was much more room on the downside.
May Brent last traded on SIMEX at $18.32 per barrel, down 19 cents from London. Earlier it traded as low as $18.26, the lowest front-month Brent price since June 26, 1996.
Brokers said the market was oversold technically following Wednesday's sell-off and better reflected the soft physical markets.
But they said traders would be cautious about taking fresh short positions ahead of the weekend when intraday players might be tempted to square positions, which would support the market.
In addition, the NYMEX crude for May has rebounded on ACCESS after the day-earlier sell off.
May NYMEX crude was last traded at an intraday high of $19.65, up 18 cents from New York.
Brokers said they expected Brent to adopt an $18.00-$18.50 range and NYMEX a $19.35-$20.00 range for the time being.
